events.subtitle: First Japan appearance in eight years with longtime collaborators
events.category: Creative jazz / eight-year Japan return / long-running international collaboration
lineup: Jun Miyake — tenor saxophone, flute, shakuhachi, nohkan
events.factual_description: Shinjuku PIT INN presents Pheeroan akLaff Quintet on Monday, October 19, 2026. Doors open at 19:00 and the performance starts at 19:30. Reserved admission is ¥5,500 and same-day admission is ¥6,050, both including one drink. The announced quintet is Pheeroan akLaff on drums, Aska Maret on violin, Toshiki Nagata on bass, Tom Pierson on piano, and Jun Miyake on tenor saxophone, flute, shakuhachi and nohkan. PIT INN explicitly states that this is akLaff's first visit to Japan in eight years and that he has assembled trusted musicians with whom he has performed over many years. Jun Miyake's official archive documents a September 16, 2013 Shinjuku PIT INN performance of akLaff's Dear Freedom Suite with Aska Kaneko, Miyake and Nagata; Arts for Art's akLaff biography separately lists recorded work with both Tom Pierson and Aska Maret-Kaneko. Seed Artists identifies akLaff as a drummer, composer, bandleader and educator with an international performance and recording history; no farewell, final-performance or premiere claim is published for the October 2026 date.

en.why_it_matters: The hook is the return, not the résumé. After eight years away from Japan, akLaff is reconvening collaborators with real shared history: Miyake's archive puts akLaff, Miyake and Nagata together at this same room in 2013, while Arts for Art documents his work with Tom Pierson and Aska Maret-Kaneko. The 2026 quintet stretches the palette from violin and piano to Miyake's tenor, flute, shakuhachi and nohkan around akLaff's drums. It is a chance to hear a long-running international creative-music network come back together in the close quarters where part of that history already happened.
en.trip_verdict: If October 19 overlaps with Tokyo, actively make room for Shinjuku and let PIT INN anchor the evening. The eight-year Japan return makes the date unusually worthwhile while you are there; without a farewell or one-off claim, I would not reroute an entire Japan trip solely for this performance.

es.why_it_matters: El gancho es el regreso, no el currículum. Después de ocho años sin tocar en Japón, akLaff vuelve a reunir colaboradores con historia compartida real: el archivo de Miyake coloca a akLaff, Miyake y Nagata juntos en esta misma sala en 2013, mientras Arts for Art documenta su trabajo con Tom Pierson y Aska Maret-Kaneko. El quinteto de 2026 abre una paleta que va del violín y el piano al tenor, la flauta, el shakuhachi y el nohkan de Miyake alrededor de la batería de akLaff. Es la oportunidad de escuchar cómo una red internacional de música creativa de largo recorrido vuelve a encontrarse en la cercanía de una sala donde parte de esa historia ya ocurrió.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 19 de octubre coincide con Tokio, sí le haría espacio a Shinjuku y dejaría que PIT INN ancle la noche. El regreso a Japón después de ocho años vuelve la fecha especialmente valiosa estando allá; sin anuncio de despedida ni de función única, no desviaría un viaje completo a Japón sólo por esta presentación.
